key_insight: Generalized pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution enables exact, high-throughput simulation of noisy quantum circuits with general Kraus channels and mid-circuit measurements.
engineering_relevance: The GPU-based CUDA-Q extension accelerates realistic quantum-error-correction data generation without relying on noise approximations such as Pauli twirling.
method: Partially pre-sample stochastic events before state evolution.
Resolve deferred outcomes during grouped execution using multinomial branching.
Reuse cached states to reduce repeated simulation work.
evidence_signal: Reported speedups over conventional CUDA-Q trajectory sampling reach 24× for distance-3 topological code memories and 83× for 30-qubit random circuits; Pauli twirling overestimated detection rates by 21% and increased lookup-decoder logical error rates by 8% in a surface-code memory comparison.
watch_item: Reported speedups are workload-specific; performance and GPU memory requirements should be validated for larger circuits and different branching patterns.
paper_title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
